source_title: Tesla, Inc. - Form 10-K (Fiscal Year 2018), with Model 3 'production hell' context
publisher_issuer: Tesla, Inc. (filed with U.S. SEC, EDGAR CIK 0001318605; corroborated by CEO statements and named journalism)
company_context: Tesla's 2017-2018 Model 3 ramp ('production hell') combined surging revenue with severe operational bottlenecks and a cash crisis. CEO Elon Musk later said Tesla came within roughly a single-digit number of weeks / about a month of bankruptcy during the ramp before reaching profitability in the second half of 2018.
macro_context: No broad macro crisis; the stress was company-specific (Model 3 mass-production scale-up). Capital markets were open, allowing Tesla to fund the bottleneck while ramping output.
outcome_category: 7 - high revenue but cash flow crisis
evidence_summary: During the Model 3 ramp Tesla was, per Musk, 'bleeding money like crazy' and within 'single-digit weeks' / about a month of bankruptcy, even as revenue scaled rapidly. Full-year 2018 total revenues were $21,461,268 thousand (~$21.46 billion). After resolving the production bottleneck, Tesla turned profitable in Q3 2018 with net income of about $311.5 million, and ended 2018 with about $3.69 billion of cash and cash equivalents, demonstrating that the crisis was an operational/cash-timing bottleneck rather than a demand failure.

source_backed_metrics.ceo_stated_proximity_to_bankruptcy: about a month / single-digit weeks during Model 3 ramp

owner_decision_context: Facing a make-or-break production bottleneck, management (Musk) chose to throw maximal resources at fixing Model 3 manufacturing (personally running the battery line, building a temporary 'GA4' assembly tent, working continuously) while managing cash tightly, betting that solving production would convert revenue growth into positive cash flow before liquidity ran out.
action_taken: Concentrated effort on breaking the Model 3 production bottleneck (line redesign, added capacity including a tent line) and tight cash management during the ramp, reaching the production rate that turned Q3 2018 to a ~$311.5M profit and ended 2018 with ~$3.69B cash.
outcome_evidence: Tesla scaled 2018 revenue to ~$21.46B, posted a ~$311.5M Q3 2018 net profit after the bottleneck eased, and held ~$3.69B cash at year-end 2018, surviving a near-bankruptcy cash crisis driven by an operational ramp rather than weak demand.
source_limitations: WebFetch of sec.gov returned 403; the FY2018 revenue ($21,461,268K), Q3 2018 net income (~$311.5M), and year-end 2018 cash (~$3.69B) are confirmed verbatim in WebSearch snippets attributed to Tesla's FY2018 10-K. The near-bankruptcy framing is Musk's own statement (CNBC, Axios, The Driven), not a 10-K figure, and is labeled as a CEO claim, not a company-reported metric.
directly_stated: Tesla's full-year 2018 total revenues were $21,461,268 thousand (~$21.46 billion)
Tesla posted Q3 2018 net income of approximately $311.5 million
Tesla had approximately $3.69 billion of cash and cash equivalents at December 31, 2018
Elon Musk stated Tesla came within about a month / single-digit weeks of bankruptcy during the Model 3 ramp
inferred: The crisis was an operational bottleneck (production scale-up) creating a cash-timing crunch, not a demand or revenue problem
Resolving the manufacturing constraint converted revenue growth into positive operating cash flow and pulled Tesla back from insolvency
why_useful_for_opsiq: Distinctive high-revenue-but-cash-crisis (outcome 7) case where the root cause is an operational/production bottleneck rather than weak demand or pure leverage. Tests whether the engine can diagnose operational_bottleneck as the driver of a cash crisis amid rapid revenue growth, and credit fixing throughput (not raising prices or cutting demand spend) as the phase-correct intervention.
